name: Purple-throated Woodstar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern panama (darién) to western colombia and southwestern ecuador
description: Woodstars are tiny hummingbirds that fly like bumblebees. Purple-throated is restricted to the west slope of the Andes in Colombia and Ecuador, where it inhabits cloud forest, edges, and second growth from 800–2,000 m.

name: Lovely Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (balabac, busuanga, culion, and palawan)
description: A tiny bird of wooded areas from the lowlands to the mountains of Palawan and neighboring islands. Has a fairly long, curved bill, a whitish belly, and olive wings.

name: Nkulengu Rail
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone to northeastern democratic republic of the congo and gabon
description: A large brown rail with a paler face and throat, blood-red legs, red eyes, and a brown bill with a paler tip. Could be mistaken for a francolin, but note short tail and secretive behavior.

name: Sunda Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Malay peninsula, and greater and lesser sundas
description: Typical Cuculus cuckoo: most adults are gray with black stripes on a white breast and belly, but some females are “hepatic”; they appear rufous overall with extensive barring. Virtually identical to Himalayan and Oriental cuckoos, which migrate through and winter in Sunda’s range; look for Sunda’s more contrasting darker gray upperparts, wider bars on the underparts, and buffier unmarked vent.

name: Creamy-bellied Antwren
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of peru (huánuco to cusco)
description: Small antwren found in the canopy of foothill forests of the eastern Andes in central Peru. Note the black cap, striped face, white wingbars, and lack of rufous in the wing.

name: Tessmann's Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of ivory coast to southern cameroon and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A plain, strong-billed rainforest flycatcher that is dark gray and black on the upperparts and pale below. Sometimes shows a vague darker gray band across the breast.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Eastern Kingbird
rangeDescription: Eastern north america; winters mainly western amazon basin
description: Fairly large flycatcher, dark gray above and clean white below with blacker head. Look for white tail tip.

name: Grenada Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southern lesser antilles (st. vincent and the grenadines, and grenada)
description: A medium-sized “fly-catching” species of open woodlands and scrub including towns, preferring areas near palms; often sits still on perch for long periods of time before leaping forth in pursuit of insects. Grenada Flycatcher has a dull brown back and a yellow belly that contrasts with its gray chest and throat.

name: Bismarck Crow
rangeDescription: Bismarck archipelago
description: A medium-sized entirely black crow with a large, often pale-tipped bill and a pale bluish eye. Common in most open forest and forest-edge habitats.

name: Morrison's Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Active small songbird, endemic to Taiwan. Brown above, white below, with gray head, large white eyering, thin black borders in crown (hard to see at times), and buffy wash in flanks.

name: Three-wattled Bellbird
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of nicaragua to western panama
description: Male is unmistakable. Body dark rufous, head and breast gleaming white, with three bare wattles hanging down off the bill.

name: Liben Lark
rangeDescription: Southern ethiopia (liben plain) and highlands of northwestern somalia
description: Looks superficially similar to a typical lark, but a careful look reveals an odd shape: a flat, triangular head, a chunky bill, a long neck, and a relatively short tail. There is a beautiful scalloped pattern on the back and thick streaking on the breast.

name: Saunders's Gull
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern china; winters south korea and southern japan to northern vietnam
description: Elegant, dark-hooded gull, restricted to coastal East Asia. Small but stout-bodied and long-winged, with a dark bill in all plumages.

name: Red-breasted Paradise-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Locally in mangroves and forest of new guinea
description: A striking, long-tailed kingfisher of lowland and foothill forest, including mangroves and riverine forest. Red bill and rump, deep orange underparts, black upperparts with blue crown, shoulder and long tail with 2 white spatules.

name: Magenta-throated Woodstar
rangeDescription: Highlands of northern costa rica and western panama
description: Tiny hummingbird with long tail often cocked up. Slow bumblebee-like flight.

name: Pacific Elaenia
rangeDescription: Western ecuador (western esmeraldas and manabí) to northwestern peru
description: A plain flycatcher restricted to dry and semi-humid forest in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru. It is best identified by the pale eyebrow and the dark, smudgy stripe that starts behind the eye and curls down behind the ear.

name: White-throated Earthcreeper
rangeDescription: West slope of andes of southwestern peru and far northern chile (arica)
description: Fairly common but local in higher foothills of the Andes. Found in scrubby valleys, often in villages and adjacent agricultural terraces.

name: Tawny-headed Swallow
rangeDescription: Venezuela and northern brazil; brazil south of the amazon river to northern argentina
description: Diminutive swallow of grasslands and savanna, particularly near water, where it occurs on its own or in small groups. Note the cinnamon head and breast contrasting with a brown back and white belly.

name: Orange Chat
rangeDescription: Interior of australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Brightly colored, terrestrial songbird found in open and arid regions across much of inland Australia. Male has rich bright orange head and underparts, with a dramatic throat that extends to the dark eye.
imageCreditName: Laurie Ross | Tracks Birding & Photography Tours

name: Baird's Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Siberia, northern alaska to greenland; winters in andes to southern south america
description: Long-winged, long-distance migrant similar to White-rumped Sandpiper but with warmer buffy-tan plumage. Elongated body gives a horizontal impression when foraging; unique flattened oval shape when seen head-on.
